title: ENCODE · SIGN · ENCRYPT
summaryPoints: Encoding changes the format; anyone can reverse it, so it protects nothing.
Signing adds a tag only a key holder can create, so changes are detected, but the message stays readable.
Encryption hides the message so only a key holder can read it.
Base64 is not encryption, and a signature is not secrecy.

chapters.name: HOOK
chapters.summary: Encoding, signing and encryption sound alike but solve three different problems.

chapters.name: ENCODING
chapters.summary: Encoding changes the format; there is no key, so anyone can undo it.

chapters.name: SIGNING
chapters.summary: A signature proves the message was not changed; the message stays readable.

chapters.name: ENCRYPTION
chapters.summary: Encryption hides the message; only the key holder can read it.

chapters.name: VERDICT
chapters.summary: Encoding is format, signing is trust, encryption is secrecy.
